Subject: Re: sudden drop in checkout success rate (May 22) — request for remedy and RCA

Hi Priyom,

We saw a 7.2% drop in successful checkouts between 16:42 and 17:08 UTC on May 22 — roughly a 26-minute window — which correlates to an 8% revenue hit for that hour. Our payment gateway logs show an increase in 503s and a spike in client-side retries during that interval. Can you confirm whether this is visible on Redwood's side as an availability delta eligible under the SLO?

We would like Redwood to:
- Confirm the impacted window and whether this meets the SLO definition for partial availability.
- Provide a preliminary credit calculation (proportional remedy) we can include with our finance team.
- Share a post-incident timeline and invite us to the postmortem call (we'd expect an RCA within 7 business days).

I've attached a small bundle with our aggregated gateway traces and a CSV of failed checkout ids (streamline_request_logs_20270522.zip). Please let us know if you need full packet captures; we'll share via secure transfer.

Thanks,
Tom Blake
Head of Ops | Streamline Payments

- Diego will pull the serving-side traces and look for 5xx counts and routing fallbacks in the 16:30–17:15 UTC window.

We'll also kick off a telemetry drill to extract the raw token-level traces and router logs. I'll send a secure upload path if you need to send full packet captures. Postmortem scheduling: we're available next Tuesday or Wednesday afternoon US-Pacific; please let us know what works for your team.

On Sat, May 22, 2027 at 17:45, priyom_das <priyom@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Diego will pull the serving-side traces and look for 5xx counts and routing fallbacks in the 16:30–17:15 UTC window.

Team / Tom — quick preliminary from my end after an initial telemetry extraction:
- We see a cluster of elevated 502/503 responses from one coloc region (us-west-2a) between 16:41:36 and 17:07:58 UTC.
- The serving runtime experienced an autoscaler backoff event triggered by an internal healthcheck flap; that caused an uneven drain while requests were routed to smaller-capacity pools.
- Automatic fallback routed some traffic to a lower-capacity variant which increased per-request latency and elevated transient 5xx rates.

This looks to meet the SLO partial-availability definition for that region and window. I'm attaching a sanitized extraction (see redwood_telemetry_pull_request_4782.json) with the exact per-shard counts.

Next steps I propose:
1) Agree on the impact window: 2027-05-22T16:41:36Z — 2027-05-22T17:07:58Z (approx).
2) Laura to compute a proportional remedy based on the SLO terms in the contract (we'll use the same revenue-at-risk approach you provided).
3) Schedule a postmortem (30–45 minutes) to review root cause and compensating actions. We recommend including service owners for autoscaler and routing.

Tom, can you confirm that the window above aligns with IDs in your CSV? If yes, we'll move to formal remedy math and a draft RCA.

— Diego
Diego Fernandez | Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
